routes.name: Tunisia Entry Visa Rules by Nationality
routes.summary: Tunisia's foreign ministry says visa rules depend on your nationality and publishes a country-by-country table (visa needed or not). If you need a visa, you apply in person at a Tunisian embassy or consulate where you live and explain why you're traveling.

other: The ministry's table of visa-exempt and visa-required countries is a PDF linked from its visa page. We couldn't read its contents here, so check your nationality there before booking.

steps: Check your nationality in the ministry's visa regime table
If a visa is needed, apply in person at the Tunisian embassy or consulate in your country of residence
Explain the reason and conditions of your trip

routes.name: Tourist, Business and Transit Visas
routes.summary: If your nationality needs a visa, you apply at a Tunisian embassy. Tourist needs a hotel booking or a notarized invitation from your host. Business needs an official invitation letter from the host. Transit needs a cruise or flight ticket. Figures below are from the embassy in Washington, DC. Other embassies may differ.

other: Passport valid at least 6 months, plus a copy of the photo page and one recent photo
Tourist visa needs approval from the Minister of Interior (per the US embassy)
In the US, applicants must show a green card or other proof of legal status in the US
The US embassy says B1/B2 visa holders can't apply for a Tunisian entry visa from the US
Stay length is not stated on the embassy page

documents: Passport (valid 6+ months) and copy of first page
Proof of legal status in the US (US applicants)
Hotel reservation or notarized invitation (tourist), official business invitation (business), cruise or airline ticket (transit)
Prepaid Priority Mail Express return envelope

routes.processing: Up to 21 business days at the US embassy. Fees are non-refundable.
